title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, officers, employees and contractors of the Company and its subsidiaries; subject to parts 3 (trading windows), 5 (exceptional circumstances) and 6 (permitted dealings) but not the part 4 notification or part 7 further restrictions (margin lending, short-term trading, hedging), which apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: All directors, officers and other key management personnel (including the CEO and CFO), and any other person designated by the Board (excluding professional/institutional investor representatives); subject to part 4 (prior notification) and part 7 (no margin lending, no short-term/speculative trading or short selling, no hedging).

tiers.name: Directors, alternate directors, CEO, CFO and Company Secretary
tiers.description: Designated Persons other than the Chairman; distinguished for clearance only: notify and obtain the Chairman's response before dealing.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman; distinguished for clearance only: notifies the other Directors before dealing.

tiers.name: Other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons other than directors, alternate directors, the CEO, CFO and Company Secretary; distinguished for clearance only: notify the Company Secretary before dealing.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Family members, trusts, companies, self-managed super funds, nominees and other persons over whom a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence, or in whom the Designated Person has an interest; the Designated Person must communicate with the Notification Officer on the Associate's behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: has not vested; or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The Company's Securities expressly includes derivative products such as OTC options; ordinary Personnel (non-Designated) may deal within an open trading window without prior notification, subject to not possessing Inside Information.
rules.evidence: the Company's Securities include any derivative products (such as warrants, exchange traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference) issued over or in respect of shares and options of the Company.

rules.detail: Dealing in the Company's Securities (including derivatives) requires prior written notice to the Notification Officer and confirmation of no Inside Information; separately, dealing 'at any time' in third-party financial products associated with the Company's Securities is banned except to the extent otherwise permitted under this policy, i.e. via a compliant window/notification dealing.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions with anyone that could limit exposure to risk relating to unvested remuneration securities.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: has not vested.

rules.detail: The same ban extends to remuneration securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The 7.3(a) hedging ban is limited to unvested/holding-locked remuneration; once vested and unlocked, a hedge implemented via third-party financial products is only restricted by the general 7.3(b) ban, which is satisfied if the dealing fits a type already permitted by the policy (window-compliant, notified dealing).
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Part 7 (which contains the hedging ban) applies only to Designated Persons, not to ordinary Personnel.

Monetisation is not separately named, but the hedging ban's effects-based test ('could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk') sweeps in a prepaid forward or similar structure over unvested remuneration securities.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: has not vested.

rules.detail: The same effects-based ban extends to vested, holding-locked remuneration securities.
rules.evidence: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: A monetisation structure using third-party financial products over vested, unlocked shares falls to the general 7.3(b) ban, satisfied by dealing within a permitted window with notification.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Part 7 does not apply to ordinary Personnel.
Outright ban on short selling for Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to engage in short selling of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: The short-selling ban is in Part 7 and applies only to Designated Persons.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are expressly within the Company's Securities definition; ordinary Personnel may deal within an open trading window without notification.
rules.evidence: the Company's Securities include any derivative products (such as warrants, exchange traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference) issued over or in respect of shares and options of the Company.

rules.detail: CFDs are expressly listed as financial products issued by third parties; banned for Designated Persons except to the extent otherwise permitted under this policy (window-compliant, notified dealing, and not hedging unvested/locked remuneration).
rules.evidence: Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on margin lending arrangements for Designated Persons, on the stated ground that terms may compel a sale during a Prohibited Period or while holding Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban is in Part 7 and applies only to Designated Persons.

The margin lending ban is expressly stated not to extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities are included as security in an ordinary lending scenario; Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if unsure how an arrangement should be classified. Granting security is not itself defined as 'dealing', so it does not independently trigger Part 4 notification.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security in an ordinary lending scenario.

rules.detail: Part 7 does not apply to ordinary Personnel, and granting security is not addressed for them at all.
Secured financing structured as a margin lending arrangement is banned outright for Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Secured financing that is an 'ordinary lending scenario' (not a margin lending arrangement) using the Company's Securities as security is expressly excluded from the prohibition.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security in an ordinary lending scenario.

rules.detail: Part 7 does not apply to ordinary Personnel.
Ban on short term or speculative trading, defined as less than a 12 month period, extending to financial products associated with the Company's Securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means in less than a 12 month period.

rules.detail: The short-term/speculative trading ban is in Part 7 and applies only to Designated Persons.

exceptions.approver: Notification Officer (Chairman for directors/CEO/CFO/Company Secretary; other Directors for the Chairman; Company Secretary for others)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, for example, a pressing and not personally induced financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant the Company's Securities.
requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements.

exceptions.approver: the Chairman (or Chief Executive Officer where the Chairman is involved)
exceptions.evidence: other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Chairman (or Chief Executive Officer where the Chairman is involved).

(superannuation) transfers of the Company's Securities which are already held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Personnel is a beneficiary (except for a self-managed superannuation fund under the control of the Personnel).

(third parties) an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

(other trustees) where the Personnel is a trustee, trading in the Company's Securities by the respective trust provided the Personnel is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Personnel.
(takeover) undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy back.
(pro rata issue) a disposal of rights acquired, or an acquisition of the Company's Securities, under a pro rata issue.

(SPPs and DRPs) trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back.

(lender disposal) a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement, where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.

(incentive scheme) the exercise (but not the sale of the Company's Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Prohibited Period.

(trading plan) trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... the trading plan does not permit the Personnel to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.
(bonus issue) acquiring the Company's Securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of the Company's Securities of the same class.

(beneficial interest) trading the Company's Securities where the trading results in no change in beneficial interest in the Company's Securities. However, the requirements of paragraphs 4.1 to 4.2 must be complied with.
(subscription under disclosure document) subscribing for the Company's Securities under a disclosure document or an offer document issued in respect of a pro rata issue.

financing_disclosure: No standalone financing-specific disclosure trigger is stated; only the general post-dealing confirmation to the Company Secretary within three business days (clause 4.2) applies once an actual dealing in the Company's Securities occurs.

exemption_authority: The Notification Officer (Chairman for directors, alternate directors, CEO, CFO and Company Secretary; the other Directors for the Chairman; the Company Secretary for other Designated Persons and for ordinary Personnel) may give prior confirmation to deal during a Prohibited Period, or to dispose despite Part 7, in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, a court order/enforceable undertaking, or other circumstances as the Chairman, or the CEO if the Chairman is involved, determines); doubtful cases are referred to the Chairman or CEO; confidentiality of a refusal is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ordinary lending carve-out from margin lending ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security in an ordinary lending scenario. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar's loan, if structured as an ordinary secured facility rather than a margin loan with LVR-triggered calls, falls outside the 7.1 prohibition entirely for Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement, where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's loan is an ordinary secured facility (not a margin loan), its enforcement sale on default is an exempt dealing usable at any time including a Prohibited Period; structuring it as a margin loan forfeits both the 7.1 permission and this exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy. Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put/call for a Designated Person must independently fit within a dealing type the policy otherwise permits (an open trading window with prior notification, or an exceptional-circumstances approval); it is not exempted merely by being off-market or third-party issued.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/locked remuneration
bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: has not vested; or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once remuneration securities vest and any holding lock lifts, the hedging-specific ban no longer applies by its terms, and the collar is then assessed only under the general financial-products restriction (7.3(b)), satisfied by ordinary window-compliant, notified dealing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Part 7 restrictions do not apply to ordinary Personnel
bespoke_clauses.clause: part 4 (prior notification) and part 7 (further restrictions) apply to all directors, officers and other key management personnel of the Company (including the CEO and CFO), and any other persons designated by the board ... ('Designated Person').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An employee holding vested shares who is not a Designated Person faces none of the margin lending, hedging, short-selling or short-term trading restrictions in Part 7, and needs no prior notification to deal, only compliance with the trading windows and the insider trading prohibition.

summary: For a Designated Person, a funded collar is workable if the loan is structured as an 'ordinary lending scenario' rather than a margin loan: clause 7.1 bans only margin lending arrangements and expressly carves out other secured funding using the shares as security, and the lender-disposal exemption in clause 6(g) likewise excludes margin loans but otherwise permits a secured lender's enforcement sale at any time, including during a Prohibited Period. The hedging ban (7.3(a)) only bites while the underlying remuneration securities are unvested or holding-locked; once vested and unlocked, the collar's put/call legs are third-party 'financial products' under clause 7.4 and are permitted only to the extent they fit a dealing type the policy already allows, in practice meaning dealt within an open trading window (post-results, post-AGM, prospectus, or cleansing-notice windows) after prior written notice to the Notification Officer and confirmation of no Inside Information, with post-trade confirmation to the Company Secretary within three business days. Outside a window, an exceptional-circumstances approval for severe hardship or a legal requirement is needed. Personnel who are not Designated Persons face none of the Part 7 restrictions at all and can deal, including in derivatives, within an open window without prior notification. The structure is achievable but turns entirely on characterising the loan as non-margin secured financing, since both the prohibition and its associated forced-sale exemption hinge on that label.
